# Continual-ARC: color cells between aligned markers

Observed task family from task-9bf5ee0c, confirmed correct on the test after three demo pairs:

- Identify the two dominant colors: background/line color and the sparse marker color.
- Scan each row and each column independently. Whenever two or more markers of the same color occur on one straight row/column, recolor the *intervening cells* between consecutive marker positions with color 2. Preserve the markers and all cells outside those spans. This applies irrespective of which color is background: recolor cells of the other color lying between markers. Do not fill arbitrary empty/background space beyond a marker.
- Equivalent implementation: for every row/column, for each consecutive pair of marker cells, set positions strictly between them to 2; leave endpoints unchanged. Union horizontal and vertical fills. If spans overlap, 2 is fine; do not change cells that are themselves marker endpoints.

Evidence from demos: in 0-background/9-marker example, gaps between 9 markers horizontally and vertically became 2; in 9-background/0-marker example, intervening 9s between 0 markers became 2. In the solved 1-background/0-marker test, intervening 1s between 0s became 2, including horizontal runs on row 11 and vertical runs in columns 1 and 17. Early incorrect attempts came from recoloring markers or filling all background; preserve marker cells and only recolor the cells strictly between aligned markers.
